bull_thesis: KBR at $35.72 is a two-business company priced as one mediocre one, with a board-committed separation about to force the market to value the parts. The company earns roughly $7.8B in revenue across two very different segments: Mission Technology Solutions (about $5.6B of revenue, roughly 10% profit margins on an adjusted cash-earnings basis, $19.1B of backlog and options up 15% year over year, essentially no contract re-competes due in 2026), and Sustainable Technology Solutions (about $2.2B of revenue at 20%-plus margins — an asset-light engineering and technology-licensing franchise in ammonia, LNG and sustainable aviation fuel, with backlog up 9% year over year and roughly 80% of its pipeline from repeat customers). The whole company trades near 8x enterprise value to trailing cash operating earnings while its closest peers (Jacobs, AECOM, Tetra Tech) trade in the 10-13x range, and the stock offers a trailing free-cash-flow yield near 11%. The catalyst is dated and in motion: the spin-off of the Mission Technology business is targeted for distribution in the second half of 2026, the spin entity's CEO and CFO were named on June 25, 2026 with start dates in July and September, and management has explicitly said it is 'open to approaches' — meaning a sale of the segment at a premium remains a live alternative path. Meanwhile the operating engine keeps delivering the part management can control: margins expanded more than 100 basis points in 2025, cash conversion ran at 110-130% of earnings, the company has beaten earnings estimates seven quarters in a row (including the April 2026 quarter at $0.96 versus $0.92 expected), and 2026 guidance was reaffirmed in May. New awards keep landing — an $8B-ceiling, 20-year Antarctic support contract from the National Science Foundation in June 2026, a $95M Space Force digital-engineering award, and three commercial-scale sustainable-aviation-fuel technology wins in six weeks. Sentiment is washed out: the shares are down about 45% over the past year, the average analyst target sits at the current price, and open-market insider buying has picked up. For the thesis to work, three things must hold: the spin distributes on schedule in the second half of 2026, Mission Technology's award-to-revenue conversion improves as the enacted 2026 defense budget flows, and Sustainable Technology's margins stay near 20% as the Plaquemines LNG joint-venture earnings wind down.
bear_thesis: The cheapness is partly an illusion of timing, and the balance sheet leaves little room for error. First, the earnings cliff: a large slice of 2025-26 profits comes from the Plaquemines LNG joint venture, whose milestone-driven earnings management itself says will run at a lower pace through 2026 with only 'spillover' into 2027 — so trailing cash flow (about $489M over the last twelve months) overstates the durable run-rate, which is why a discounted-cash-flow model on trailing numbers produces a fair value near $21 while an asset-based view produces the mid-$40s. Second, the revenue engine is stalled: 2025 revenue grew less than 1%, the April 2026 quarter was down 5% year over year with earnings per share down 9%, and management has now promised an award-cadence pickup 'in the second half' for four consecutive quarters while $17B of bids sit un-awarded and protested contracts drag on. Third, credibility on the top line is genuinely damaged: in May 2025 management called the HomeSafe relationship with its military customer 'strong' and expressed confidence in the program's future; one quarter later the contract was terminated on them. Fourth, leverage: $2.49B of net debt is about 2.9x cash operating earnings, tangible book value is negative, and the solvency screen sits in the grey zone (Altman-Z 2.5) — manageable for an asset-light services firm, but a spin-off splits the cash flows that service that debt, and how the debt is allocated between the two companies is not yet disclosed. Fifth, spins are not free money: the remaining and spun entities routinely see mechanical selling as index funds and mandate-constrained holders exit, and the value case then depends on two smaller companies each earning a better multiple than the market currently awards the whole — precisely what the peer comparison says is not obviously mispriced today. What would confirm the bear: a Q2 print on July 30, 2026 that trims guidance, a spin timeline slipping into 2027, or Sustainable Technology margins falling back toward mid-teens as the LNG joint-venture earnings fade.
sop_breakdown: Sum-of-the-parts (valuing each business line separately), built on corrected fiscal-2025 segment figures — note the screener's segment feed materially understated Mission Technology revenue ($1.34B shown versus roughly $5.58B actual, which is total revenue of $7.79B minus Sustainable Technology's $2.21B). Base case: Mission Technology Solutions, ~$5.6B revenue at ~10% adjusted cash-earnings margin gives ~$550M, valued at 9x (a discount to defense-services peers for the current award drought) = ~$5.0B. Sustainable Technology Solutions, ~$2.2B revenue at 20%-plus margins gives ~$450M including joint-venture earnings; haircutting for the fading Plaquemines LNG contribution to ~$400M durable and valuing at 11x (asset-light licensing quality, below pure technology-licensing peers) = ~$4.4B. Unallocated corporate costs of roughly $90-100M a year, capitalized at ~9x = about -$0.9B. That sums to ~$8.5B of enterprise value; subtracting $2.49B net debt (recomputed from the April 2026 balance sheet) leaves ~$6.0B of equity, or about $46 on ~127M shares. The bear case ($29.50) uses 8x on a stalled Mission Technology at $500M and 9x on a $350M ex-LNG Sustainable Technology, landing at the 52-week low. The bull case ($58) assumes a clean separation re-rates both parts toward peer multiples (10x and 12.5x respectively) with partial corporate-cost elimination — still below the $59-88 range circulating in published sum-of-the-parts work. This base case independently corroborates the screener's own $46.5 fair-value anchors.
risk_reward: Downside in an adverse scenario is anchored near the 52-week low around $29-30, where the stock already traded during the June 2026 washout and where the bear-case parts valuation lands. Upside to the base-case sum-of-the-parts sits in the mid-$40s, with the favorable case in the high-$50s if the separation completes cleanly and both companies re-rate toward peer multiples. The spread is asymmetric in the buyer's favor at today's $35.72, but the risk is concentrated in the next two quarters: the July 30, 2026 earnings print and the spin execution window both land before the value can be realized.
peer_comps_note: The house peer set is Fluor, Jacobs, AECOM, Tetra Tech and MasTec, with Jacobs the closest true comp; the peer file's verdict is that KBR trades roughly in line — the market pays for government-backlog stability while discounting lumpy project cash flow. Live check supports the discount narrowing case rather than a screaming outlier: KBR's trailing enterprise-value-to-cash-operating-earnings multiple is about 8.2x versus roughly 10-13x for the diversified engineering peers, and its free-cash-flow yield near 11% is the highest in the group — but part of that gap is the fading LNG joint-venture earnings and the 2.9x net-debt load, so the honest read is 'cheap with an explanation', where the spin is the mechanism that tests whether the explanation is worth the full 20-plus-percent discount.
forcing_function: Three dated events force the re-rating. First and largest: the distribution of the Mission Technology Solutions spin-off, targeted for the second half of 2026 — execution is visibly under way, with the spin entity's CFO-designate starting July 1, 2026 and CEO-designate on September 24, 2026, and the registration and record-date announcements that precede a distribution are the next hard markers. Second: the second-quarter earnings call on July 30, 2026, which will carry a spin progress update and is the first test of the reaffirmed 2026 guidance. Third: the open question management pointedly declined to close in February 2026 — whether the Mission Technology business is sold outright rather than spun ('we're open to approaches') — any strategic-sale headline would reprice the parts immediately.
moderator_conclusion: KBR is a legitimate sum-of-the-parts discount with a real, dated corporate catalyst — and a set of honest reasons the market is skeptical. The base-case value of about $46 per share against a $35.72 price is corroborated three ways: our segment build, the screener's own fair-value models, and independent published work that lands even higher. The catalyst is a hard, scheduled corporate event: a board-committed separation targeted for the second half of 2026 with leadership already hired, and a possible outright sale as a premium alternative. Management's delivery on margins and cash is excellent (seven straight earnings beats, 110-130% cash conversion, 100-plus basis points of margin expansion in 2025), which supports the value floor. What holds this to a wait-for-the-washout stance rather than an aggressive entry: top-line credibility is genuinely impaired (the HomeSafe termination blindside, four quarters of promised award pickups that keep slipping), a meaningful slice of trailing earnings comes from an LNG joint venture that fades after 2026, net debt at 2.9x cash earnings must be split across two smaller companies, and the July 30 earnings print plus the mechanical index selling that accompanies most spin distributions offer a plausible better entry in the next one to two quarters. The specific event to wait for: either a post-earnings or spin-distribution flush toward the low-$30s, or the record-date announcement that hardens the timeline — at which point the discount has a forced closing mechanism and the position deserves an upgrade. On management quality: a deep dive across five quarters of calls scores credibility 3 out of 5 — high reliability on profit and cash guidance, low-to-medium on revenue promises — with the company's trajectory best described as turning: deliberately splitting itself in two after a bruising year to force the value question.

skeptic_self.kill_fact: Two material corrections were applied before scoring. (1) The input's segment-revenue block inverted the business mix: it showed Mission Technology at $1.34B (38% of revenue) when fiscal-2025 actuals put it near $5.58B (~72%) — the FMP segment feed captured only a partial figure; the sum-of-the-parts was rebuilt on corrected revenue and margin weights. (2) Trailing cheapness is overstated: the ~$489M trailing free cash flow and 20%-plus Sustainable Technology margins embed Plaquemines LNG joint-venture milestone earnings that management guides to fade through 2026 with only spillover into 2027, so the durable earnings base is smaller than the trailing multiple implies. Both corrections tempered conviction from 4 to 3 and hold the catalyst-blind value score at 3 despite the optical 11% free-cash-flow yield; the HomeSafe termination blindside (management called the customer relationship 'strong' one quarter before cancellation) independently caps management credibility at 3.
